metadata.case_name: KEN JOHN GEISSLER AND ANOTHER v. CHAN KIM-CHUNG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Partner in a trading/export company called Troika International Limited; responsible for marketing

source: Some weeks later he was diagnosed to have suffered Late Whiplash Syndrome (LWS), a common injury in such an accident.
Dr Shroff's diagnosis, agreed by Dr Yu for the defendants, is that Mr Geissler has suffered LWS.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified strain or sprain of cervical spine

injuries.description: a posterior central C5-6 herniation / minor postero-central disc protrusion at C5-6 with minimal compression of the thecal sac anteriorly
source: an MRI taken at Dr Wong's request on 27 May 1998 revealed a posterior central C5-6 herniation.
A further MRI taken on 4 July 2000 describes the injury as a minor postero-central disc protrusion at C5-6 with minimal compression of the thecal sac anteriorly.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

manifestations.description: he had immediate pain in his neck
symptoms now suffered by Mr Geissler are primarily those of pain, both in his neck and by way of headaches
daily stiffness of the neck especially after sleeping with incorrect posture, or after a long international flight
He suffers headaches every ten days or so
He must work with his head erect, and needs regular breaks to avoid pain
Activities such as cooking or ironing are made difficult by pain as a result of bending
He finds reading, his favourite form of relaxation, difficult if his head is bent for long periods
He is now unable to ride a motorcycle, nor practise yoga
He has difficulty in lifting heavy weights such as a suitcase
Constant turning of his head when at a trade fair causes pain
The inability to play squash at his previous level

treatments_received: taken by ambulance to Queen Elizabeth Hospital; plain x-rays taken and treated conservatively and discharged
wearing a neck brace for a period
attendance at the Canadian Asian Back Institute (CANBI) for exercises
use of a lumbar roll to maintain posture
treatments_future: attendance at the Canadian Asian Back Institute (CANBI) for exercises
possible spinal fusion (a laminectomy) as a remote prospect

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: The inability to play squash at his previous level; he could continue only recreationally and has stopped competitive play; loss of enjoyment from playing squash at a very high previous standard

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty with ironing and sorting clothes leading to laundry being done outside home; award based on $250 a month for 25 years

losses.category: Loss of holidays or special occasions
losses.description: Discomfort on long haul international flights and on long or bumpy car journeys requiring him at times to add time to a trip to allow discomfort to ease
